grounded_facts: Dr. Wren directs Gediman to proceed carefully and prepare the amniotic chamber.
memories.memory_text: I heard Wren tell Gediman to be careful and prepare the amniotic chamber as they worked on me.

grounded_facts: Gediman announces the alien has been successfully located and extracted.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gediman say, 'There she is...' as he found and removed the alien from my body.

grounded_facts: Wren warns the team as the alien wriggles free and threatens to escape.
memories.memory_text: I heard the alien scream and wriggle free, and then Wren shouted 'Watch it!' as it nearly escaped.

grounded_facts: After confirming Ripley's vitals are stable, Wren authorizes closing the surgical incision.
memories.memory_text: After they checked my vitals and said I was doing fine, I heard Wren say, 'Sew her back up,' before they closed the incision.

grounded_facts: A medical operation conducted to extract the alien from Ripley's body.
The alien is surgically removed from Ripley's chest in an operating chamber.
memories.memory_text: I felt my chest being cut open and the alien pulled from inside me, its umbilical threads severed before it was placed in an amniotic chamber.

grounded_facts: Immediately after the alien is removed, Ripley suddenly awakens and violently attacks the surgeon.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly woke up and my hand lashed out, grabbing the surgeon's arm—I felt it crush under my grip as he yelled in pain.

grounded_facts: Ripley is held in a small, dark cell with a glass pane in the ceiling, observed by a guard from above.
memories.memory_text: I was crouching in a dark cell, barely able to see, with only a dim light coming from a glass pane above me—I could feel someone watching me from the other side.

grounded_facts: A guard looks down into Ripley's cell through a glass pane in the floor, monitoring her from above.
memories.memory_text: I crouched in the dark cell, barely moving, when I sensed someone above me—I looked up and saw the guard staring down through the glass in the ceiling, watching me.

grounded_facts: Ripley lifts her hands, touches her face and skin, inspects her tunic and chest scar, and looks at the tattoo on her forearm.
memories.memory_text: I lifted my hands and looked at them, then touched my face and skin; I pulled at my tunic and saw the scar on my chest, tracing it with my fingers, and when I looked at my forearm, I saw the number 8 tattooed near my elbow.

grounded_facts: Gediman informs Wren that Ripley's healing is extraordinary and off projected charts.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gediman tell Wren that my healing was extraordinary and completely off their projected charts, pointing out how my scar tissue had receded since yesterday.

grounded_facts: A medical check-up of Ripley involving blood draw, eye examination, and discussion of her healing progress.
memories.memory_text: I went through a medical check-up where they drew my blood, examined my eyes, and later Wren came to study my face, discussing my healing progress with satisfaction.

grounded_facts: Wren tells Ripley she will make them proud, expressing satisfaction with her progress.
memories.memory_text: I remember Wren telling me I would make them proud, right before everything inside me snapped.

grounded_facts: Ripley grabs Wren and demands to know 'why', showing emotional distress.
Ripley suddenly attacks Wren by grabbing his throat, demanding to know 'why', before being subdued by guards.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Wren by the throat and demanded to know why, my voice breaking as I stared into his face, needing an answer.

grounded_facts: After refusing to release Wren, Ripley is struck by an electrical charge from a guard's 'burner' and thrown into a corner.
memories.memory_text: I refused to let go, and then I was hit by a powerful electrical charge that threw me into the corner, leaving me stunned and helpless.

grounded_facts: Ripley exhibits extraordinary healing, with scar tissue showing significant recession in less than a day.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting on the table while Gediman drew my blood and examined my eyes, and I noticed I had recovered from the shock much faster than expected, with my scars already receding noticeably in less than a day.

grounded_facts: Ripley undergoes a cognitive assessment with picture recognition, displaying signs of frustration and boredom.
memories.memory_text: I had to sit through a picture test with a scientist showing me cards—house, dog, boat—and I felt pissed off and bored, just going through the motions.

grounded_facts: Wren and Gediman assess Ripley's cognitive and emotional condition, noting gaps in memory and emotional autism-like symptoms.
memories.memory_text: I could feel Wren and Gediman watching me through the glass, and though I knew what they were testing, I couldn't shake the sense that they saw something broken in me—like my reactions weren't right, that I was somehow off in a way they couldn't fix.

grounded_facts: A formal session in which Ripley is tested on picture recognition while observed by Wren, Gediman, and General Perez.
memories.memory_text: I knew Wren and Gediman were watching me from behind that one-way glass, and General Perez was there too, staring with suspicion; I could feel it, like I was some kind of threat they were trying to figure out.

grounded_facts: Perez watches Ripley through the one-way mirror with suspicion and exits afterward.
memories.memory_text: I noticed General Perez watching me through the glass with a suspicious look before he turned and left the room.

grounded_facts: Ripley and Gediman are seated in the mess hall, ostensibly for a meal, though Ripley is not eating.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting across from Gediman in the mess hall, not eating, while he ate and I stared at the utensil in my hand.

grounded_facts: Ripley struggles to recall the word for a utensil, triggered by Gediman, indicating memory recovery or cognitive difficulty.
memories.memory_text: I struggled to recall the word for the utensil I was holding, even though it was right there in my hand, and all I could say was 'Fuck...'.

grounded_facts: Gediman repeatedly says 'Fork' to help or test Ripley's memory, which leads to her recalling the word.
memories.memory_text: Gediman said 'Fork' to me, and then again after I didn't respond, and that's when I finally remembered the word.

grounded_facts: Wren informs Ripley that Weyland Yutani is defunct, bought out by Walmart, and that the current organization is different.
memories.memory_text: I was told Weyland Yutani went under decades ago, bought out by Walmart, and that things have changed a lot since my time.

grounded_facts: Wren attempts to justify the military's use of the alien species by emphasizing scientific and material benefits.
memories.memory_text: I was told the military isn't flying blind, that they're harnessing the aliens for new alloys and vaccines, and that I should be proud of the benefits they claim will come from them.

grounded_facts: Ripley deduces that the alien organism is a queen, implying reproductive capability and existential threat.
memories.memory_text: I realized it was a queen — I told them she'd breed and everyone in the Company would die. I called it a cancer because it can't be controlled, no matter what they think.

grounded_facts: Ripley reflects on Wren's use of 'them' and begins to grasp that more than one alien organism may be present or planned.
memories.memory_text: I heard Wren say 'them' and it hit me — there's more than one of these things, or they plan to make more. I realized it's not just a single creature; it's a breeding threat.

grounded_facts: Johner repeatedly challenges and mocks Ripley, leading to physical retaliation.
memories.memory_text: I told Johner to get away from me when he came up close and mocked me, but he just kept provoking me with that ugly smile.

grounded_facts: A late-night poker game among crew members escalates into a violent confrontation involving Ripley.
memories.memory_text: I threw the basketball hard at Call, and when Christie swung at me and smashed me in the face, I came right back at her, got her by the throat, and kept fighting even as Johner came at me—I leapt on him and threw him down, snarling, until he gasped, 'What the fuck are you?'

grounded_facts: Ripley violently repels Johner and others during a confrontation in the conference hall, revealing her enhanced physical capabilities.
memories.memory_text: I hit Johner hard enough to send him flying, then took down Christie and Hillard when they attacked me—I felt my strength surge as I choked Christie and threw Johner down again, knowing everyone was staring at me.

grounded_facts: Ripley's blood sizzles and melts a small patch on the floor, indicating non-human or corrosive properties.
memories.memory_text: I saw my blood drip and sizzle on the floor, melting a small patch, and realized it wasn't normal.

grounded_facts: Gediman monitors adult aliens in a secure pen, studying their behavior and communication patterns.
memories.memory_text: I stepped up behind Gediman while he was watching the aliens in the pen, writing notes—he didn't seem surprised to see me—I stood beside him and watched the one hissing at the glass, the others curled up and still.

grounded_facts: Ripley tells Gediman she can hear ultrasonic alien communications, indicating a unique connection.
memories.memory_text: I told Gediman I can hear them, the ultrasonic communications—he needed to know about my connection to the aliens.

grounded_facts: Call sees Ripley's chest scar and hesitates in her assassination attempt, indicating prior knowledge.
memories.memory_text: Call saw the scar on my chest and froze, her resolve breaking—she recognized me, or something about me, and couldn't go through with the kill.

grounded_facts: Call sneaks into Ripley's cell with a concealed blade, intending to kill her, but hesitates upon seeing her scar.
memories.memory_text: I saw Call sneak into my cell with a blade, intending to kill me, but she hesitated when she saw my chest scar.

grounded_facts: Ripley demonstrates her inhuman resilience by impaling her own hand with Call's stiletto and withdrawing it unharmed, reinforcing her hybrid nature.
memories.memory_text: I took Call's stiletto and impaled my own hand with it, showing her I felt no pain and wasn't like other humans.

grounded_facts: Call confronts Ripley about her true nature, accusing her of being a lab-grown construct rather than the real Ellen Ripley.
memories.memory_text: Call confronted me, telling me I wasn't the real Ellen Ripley but a lab-grown construct created to bring forth the beast.

grounded_facts: Ripley confirms that the alien entity is not fully extracted and remains active within her consciousness, able to communicate and influence thought.
memories.memory_text: I told Call the alien is still inside me, moving behind my eyes, and that I can hear it in my head.

grounded_facts: Ripley tells Call that the alien's emergence is inevitable, driven by human desire and inevitability.
memories.memory_text: I told Call the emergence of the alien is inevitable, that it will come because humanity will bring it forth out of desire.

grounded_facts: Ripley physically attacks Call by grabbing her throat, demonstrating power and delivering a cryptic warning before releasing her.
After choking Call, Ripley releases her and tells her to flee, showing a moment of restraint.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Call by the throat, squeezed until she couldn't breathe, told her I could make it stop, then released her and told her to flee before they came.

grounded_facts: The adult aliens break free by killing one of their own and using its corrosive blood to melt through the floor, then ambush and kill Gediman and a guard.
memories.memory_text: I saw the aliens turn on one of their own, tearing it apart so they could use its blood to melt through the floor; I watched in horror as they burst through the hole and killed Gediman and the guard before vanishing into the lower levels.

grounded_facts: A surprise raid on the Betty crew escalates into a violent firefight, resulting in the crew seizing control from Wren's forces.
memories.memory_text: I saw Elgyn, Hillard, and Rane pushed in, then Christie, St Just, and Johner herded in by Wren's soldiers—I watched as Elgyn pulled guns from his sleeves, asked St Just, and in a flash, St Just took out the guards and held Wren at gunpoint while Johner covered the others, then shoved a gun in Wren's mouth when more guards rushed in.

grounded_facts: Ripley reacts to the sounds of the alien outbreak with laughter, indicating psychological alignment with the destruction.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting in the dark, hearing the chaos start to build, and I just couldn't help laughing.

grounded_facts: Elgyn is killed by the Alien when it drops from the rafters and impales his skull with its tongue.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Alien drop from the rafters and impale Elgyn through the skull with its tongue—he didn’t even have time to scream.

grounded_facts: Ripley fights and kills the Alien in a brutal physical confrontation, ripping out its tongue.
memories.memory_text: I fought the Alien bare-handed, and when it lunged at me, I grabbed its tongue and ripped it out with a scream—I felt every inch of that kill.

grounded_facts: Ripley hands Call the severed Alien tongue as a disturbing souvenir, possibly in retaliation for being shot.
memories.memory_text: I handed Call the severed Alien tongue, placing it in her hand myself before walking on—she shot me, and I made sure she remembered it.

grounded_facts: Wren discloses that there are thirty Aliens aboard the ship.
memories.memory_text: I heard Wren say there are thirty Aliens aboard the ship.

grounded_facts: Christie silences Call's objections about trusting Ripley by asserting his leadership.
memories.memory_text: I saw Christie raise his voice and silence Call's objections, asserting his authority over the group.

grounded_facts: Call reveals to the group that Ripley is a clone created by Wren and may carry an Alien inside her.
memories.memory_text: I heard Call tell the group that I’m a clone created by Wren and might be carrying an Alien inside me, and that I could turn.

grounded_facts: Hillard gently places her coat over Elgyn's face as a sign of mourning.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hillard gently place her coat over Elgyn's face as a way to mourn him.

grounded_facts: Hillard moves away when Call tries to comfort her after Elgyn's death.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Hillard move away when Call tried to comfort her after Elgyn's death.

grounded_facts: Ripley gives Call a cold, unsettling smile, signaling lingering hostility.
memories.memory_text: I gave Call a cold smile when she looked back at me, letting her see the hostility I still carry.

grounded_facts: Vriess appears unexpectedly from a dark elevator, alive and armed, rejoining the surviving crew.
memories.memory_text: I saw sparks fly from the elevator ceiling and then Vriess appeared in the light, alive and armed, making everyone jump and nearly open fire before realizing it was him.

grounded_facts: Johner reveals to Vriess and the group that Call is a spy, escalating tension.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Johner that Call is a spy, which escalated the tension among the group.

grounded_facts: The group uses a holographic console to assess ship damage and plan a route to the Betty.
memories.memory_text: I used the holographic console with the group to assess the ship's damage and plan our route to the Betty, seeing the breaches and damaged sections highlighted in the hologram.

grounded_facts: Ripley reveals that the Aliens will breed rapidly, doubling in number within hours.
memories.memory_text: I told the group the Aliens will breed rapidly and double in number within hours, and that they’ll stay close to where the hosts are.

grounded_facts: Vriess distributes hidden weapons, giving a shotgun to Hillard and a grenade launcher to Call.
Vriess tosses a grenade launcher to Call without warmth, arming her for the journey.
memories.memory_text: I saw Vriess hand a shotgun to Hillard and then toss a grenade launcher to Call without saying anything warm—just cold, like he didn't trust her. He even warned her not to shoot her foot off.

grounded_facts: The group gathers at the guards' station to use the ship's console to plan their route to the Betty.
memories.memory_text: I was there when we gathered at the guards’ station and used the console to pull up the ship’s layout so we could plan our route to the Betty.

grounded_facts: The group regroups after surviving the Alien attack to assess threats, reveal information, and debate trust.
memories.memory_text: After the attack, I helped regroup the survivors, and we argued about the threat—how many more Aliens there might be and whether we could trust each other.

grounded_facts: Ripley senses the ship is moving, prompting Call to verify via the computer.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Ripley senses the ship is moving, prompting Call to verify via the computer.

grounded_facts: The ship has automatically started moving toward Earth due to damage, a fact revealed by Call and confirmed by Wren.
memories.memory_text: I was told that The ship has automatically started moving toward Earth due to damage, a fact revealed by Call and confirmed by Wren.

grounded_facts: Call angrily questions Wren for withholding knowledge that the ship would autopilot to Earth.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Call angrily questions Wren for withholding knowledge that the ship would autopilot to Earth.

grounded_facts: Christie asks Ripley to lead the group during their movement.
memories.memory_text: I was asked to take point during the group's movement, so I stepped forward to lead the way.

grounded_facts: The group finalizes their escape plan, confirms weapon readiness, and learns the ship is moving toward Earth.
memories.memory_text: I felt the ship moving and realized we were heading toward Earth, so I helped finalize the escape plan and made sure my weapon was ready.

grounded_facts: Johner asks Ripley about her prior experience with the Aliens.
memories.memory_text: I was asked by Johner if I'd faced these creatures before, and when he pressed me on what I did, I told him I died.

grounded_facts: The group moves through a destroyed lab, encountering signs of recent Alien violence.
memories.memory_text: I moved through the destroyed lab and saw the aftermath of the Alien’s attack—bodies torn open, the group scattered, and signs of violence everywhere.

grounded_facts: The group enters a trashed lab and finds three bodies with exploded chests, indicating prior Alien presence and violence.
memories.memory_text: I moved through the trashed lab and saw three bodies with their chests exploded outward, clear signs of what the Aliens had done.

grounded_facts: The group encounters Purvis, who attacks them with a metal bar out of fear, leading to a tense standoff before he is subdued and questioned.
memories.memory_text: I was attacked out of nowhere when something leapt from the shadows and a metal bar slammed into my side, and then I saw Purvis swinging the bar wildly at everyone, his eyes filled with terror before we managed to subdue him.

grounded_facts: Ripley detects that Purvis is carrying an alien organism inside his body, revealing a critical threat to the group.
memories.memory_text: I could smell it — the alien inside him — and I realized Purvis was carrying one inside his body, a hidden threat that put all of us in danger.

grounded_facts: Ripley bluntly informs Purvis that he has an alien creature inside him that will kill him by bursting from his chest.
memories.memory_text: I told Purvis directly that there was a monster in his stomach, that the smugglers had hijacked his cryotube and sold him to Wren, who implanted the alien, and that it would burst through his chest in a few hours and kill him.

grounded_facts: Call asserts command over the group's decision to save Purvis, provoking Johner's resentment and verbal confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Call take charge and say we should bring Purvis with us, and Johner challenged her, asking since when she was in charge, but Call shut him down cold.

grounded_facts: Christie warns Purvis that he will be shot if he becomes aggressive, establishing controlled escort terms.
The group decides to take the infected Purvis with them instead of killing or abandoning him, altering their risk profile and mission constraints.
memories.memory_text: I saw Christie warn Purvis that he'd be shot if he got aggressive, and I remember thinking we were all taking a risk—I didn't know if bringing him onto the Betty would save him or get us all killed.

grounded_facts: Ripley proposes throwing Call into the alien chamber as bait to lure the creatures into the trap.
memories.memory_text: I suggested using bait to get the aliens into the chamber, and I pointed at Call, telling the others we should throw her in to make them come.

grounded_facts: Wren uses the liquid nitrogen failsafe to freeze three aliens after luring them into the chamber.
memories.memory_text: I watched Wren activate the liquid nitrogen failsafe and freeze three aliens as they charged toward us.

grounded_facts: The group encounters active alien threats and devises a trap using liquid nitrogen to eliminate them.
memories.memory_text: I saw the group come up with a plan to lure the aliens into a chamber and freeze them using liquid nitrogen.

grounded_facts: Call tells Ripley she is more human than she thought, implying Ripley's willingness to sacrifice others makes her cruelly human.
memories.memory_text: I remember Call saying to me, 'I guess you're more human than I thought,' in a bitter tone, as if my choices proved something dark about me.

grounded_facts: Call hands the grenade launcher to Ripley, enabling her to destroy the clones.
Ripley enters the Cloning Storage Facility and destroys the failed Ripley clones with a grenade launcher.
memories.memory_text: I took the grenade launcher from Call and fired into the cloning chamber, watching the failed clones explode in flame—I destroyed them all, including the hybrid, with my own hands.

grounded_facts: Ripley discovers and destroys the failed clones of herself in the Cloning Storage Facility.
memories.memory_text: I found a room full of failed clones of myself, including a horrifying hybrid, and I destroyed them all with grenades.

grounded_facts: After Ripley spares Wren, Call punches him in the jaw as a warning.
memories.memory_text: After I spared Wren, I saw Call punch him in the jaw—she didn't agree with my mercy, but I made the call.

grounded_facts: The group discovers that the cooling tanks have been breached, flooding the corridor with water.
memories.memory_text: I dropped into the corridor and saw the floor was covered in dark water; Wren pointed out that it was flooding from the breached cooling tanks.

grounded_facts: The crew navigates a flooded corridor and kitchen under threat, culminating in an alien ambush and surface-level facehugger attack.
memories.memory_text: I led the group through a flooded corridor and kitchen, and I struggled underwater when an alien grabbed my foot during an ambush.

grounded_facts: The crew swims through a flooded corridor and kitchen, only to be ambushed by three aliens in the water, initiating combat and triggering a desperate escape.
memories.memory_text: I swam with the crew through the flooded corridor and kitchen, and just as we were making our way to the stairs, I saw three aliens ambush us from behind — I hurried the others past me while an alien grabbed my foot, holding me under until I kicked free and we escaped the blood spreading in the water.

grounded_facts: The group observes two aliens killing a group of soldiers, confirming the presence and threat of multiple aliens.
memories.memory_text: I saw two aliens attack and kill a group of soldiers, and I realized we were dealing with multiple deadly creatures.

grounded_facts: Di Stephano inhales water and stops breathing during underwater passage; later revives after being pulled out and receiving aid.
memories.memory_text: I saw Di Stephano inhaling water and thrashing during the swim, and after we surfaced, Hillard and Johner pulled him out — he wasn't breathing, but Call gave him mouth-to-mouth and he sputtered back to life, so I picked him up to help get him to safety.

grounded_facts: Wren, unable to open a jammed maintenance door, shoots Call through the chest to use her gun as a tool, killing her and sealing himself inside.
Wren uses Call's gun to force open a jammed door, but instead of returning it, he shoots her through the chest, killing her.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wren take Call's gun and instead of opening the door properly, he shot her through the chest, killing her and sealing himself inside while we were left locked out.

grounded_facts: An alien appears on the ledge where Ripley has just arrived; she screams and hurls herself at it, causing both to fall.
An alien emerges on the maintenance ledge near Ripley; she attacks it mid-leap, both fall, but Ripley grabs a pole and survives.
memories.memory_text: I screamed and hurled myself at the alien that rose right in front of me on the ledge, and we both went flying off—but I managed to grab a pole and hold on while it fell.

grounded_facts: As survivors break the surface, facehuggers ambush them, attempting to attach to Ripley, Wren, and others; eggs are destroyed in response.
memories.memory_text: As I broke the surface, a facehugger clamped onto my face and pulled me under — I fought it, tearing it apart, while more facehuggers attacked the others; we destroyed the eggs and saw them crawling on the aliens before they scurried off looking for new hosts.

grounded_facts: An alien grabs Christie during climb; he fires twice, killing it despite being injured by acid blood.
An alien attacks Christie during climb; he is sprayed with acid blood and loses grip, but survives after Vriess supports him and he kills the alien.
memories.memory_text: I saw Christie get grabbed by an alien during the climb, sprayed with acid blood, and lose his grip, but Vriess supported him and he managed to fire again and kill it.

grounded_facts: The final alien disengages and retreats downward after Christie is attacked, ending immediate threat.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the last alien suddenly disengage and scurry back down the shaft after the others, ending the immediate threat.

grounded_facts: Hillard cuts the cord binding Christie's body to Vriess to allow continued escape.
memories.memory_text: I saw Hillard cut the cord that was binding Christie's body to Vriess so we could keep moving.

grounded_facts: Christie's body, carried by Vriess, is confirmed dead; Hillard cuts the cord binding him to Vriess, allowing the body to fall into the shaft.
memories.memory_text: I watched Christie's body fall into the dark shaft after the cord was cut, and I knew he was gone.

grounded_facts: After Christie's body falls, two aliens are spotted ascending the shaft, prompting renewed urgency in the climb.
memories.memory_text: I heard a loud clacking from below and then saw the aliens still coming up the shaft, which made me push harder to get away.

grounded_facts: Survivors climb a vertical liftshaft under alien pursuit, facing betrayal, falls, injuries, and eventual retreat of enemies.
memories.memory_text: I climbed the liftshaft with the others while aliens pursued us, and I pulled Call to safety when an alien grabbed her ankle.

grounded_facts: Ripley fires at the lift's support cables, causing it to plummet and crush two aliens at the bottom of the shaft.
memories.memory_text: I took Hillard's shotgun and fired at the lift's support cables, making it plummet and crush two aliens at the bottom.

grounded_facts: After being pulled from the lift, Call's chest wound reveals synthetic wiring instead of blood and bone, exposing her as an artificial being.
memories.memory_text: I saw the wound on Call's chest after we pulled her up, and instead of blood and bone, there was a tangle of synthetic wiring—I realized she wasn't human.

grounded_facts: Johner ridicules Call after learning she is a synthetic, making crude jokes about her mechanical nature.
memories.memory_text: I heard Johner make a crude joke about Call needing an oil change after he found out she was a synthetic.

grounded_facts: Call reveals she burned her modem drive to prevent remote access to the ship's systems, a self-sabotage to resist forced use.
memories.memory_text: I heard Call say she burned her modem drive to stop remote access, and that they all did it.

grounded_facts: Ripley and Call enter the chapel to use its computer ports so Call can manually access the ship's mainframe and potentially trigger self-destruct.
memories.memory_text: I went with Call into the chapel so she could plug into the computer system and try to trigger the ship's self-destruct.

grounded_facts: Call reveals her forearm ports and connects a cable to access the ship's computer system manually.
memories.memory_text: I watched Call pull up her sleeve, open the panel in her forearm, and connect the cable to the ship's system so she could access it directly.

grounded_facts: Ripley pressures Call to plug into the mainframe despite her resistance, using moral leverage about Earth's safety.
memories.memory_text: I pressured Call to plug into the mainframe, even though she resisted and said it felt like her insides were liquid—I told her she could blow the ship before it reached Earth to stop them all, and that convinced her to do it.

grounded_facts: After learning Wren is approaching the ship, Ripley asks Call, 'And how do you feel about that?'
memories.memory_text: After learning Wren was approaching the ship, I asked Call, 'And how do you feel about that?'

grounded_facts: Call connects to the ship's PA system and takes control from the AI 'Father', speaking through the ship's speakers to confront Wren.
memories.memory_text: I saw Call take control of the ship's PA system from Father and speak through the speakers to confront Wren.

grounded_facts: Call uses the ship's PA system to announce 'Father's dead, asshole' to Wren, shocking and disorienting him.
memories.memory_text: I heard Call announce 'Father's dead, asshole' over the ship's system, shocking Wren.

grounded_facts: Call uses the ship's system to redirect aliens toward Wren's location, marking him as an intruder.
Call broadcasts 'Intruder on level one... all aliens please proceed to level one' through the ship's system, directing threats toward Wren.
memories.memory_text: I saw Call use the ship's system to redirect the aliens toward Wren by broadcasting 'Intruder on level one... all aliens please proceed to level one'.

grounded_facts: When Ripley offers to examine her chest wiring, Call snaps 'Don't touch me,' rejecting physical contact.
memories.memory_text: I reached out to examine Call's chest wiring, but she snapped at me not to touch her.

grounded_facts: Call confronts her synthetic nature, calling herself 'disgusting' and questioning her existence, showing emotional deterioration.
memories.memory_text: I heard Call say 'I'm disgusting' to herself after disconnecting from the mainframe, struggling with being synthetic.

grounded_facts: Ripley reveals that her nightmares about the aliens are less horrifying than reality, indicating psychological endurance.
memories.memory_text: I told Call that no matter how bad my dreams get, when I wake up, reality is always worse.

grounded_facts: Call removes the cable from her forearm port, ending her direct connection to the ship's computer system.
memories.memory_text: I think Call disconnected herself by removing the cable from her forearm port, though I didn't see it directly—she just said 'Let's get going' afterward.

grounded_facts: Ripley hesitates at the controls; Call turns on the ignition to help her start driving.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated at the controls, and Call turned on the ignition to help me start driving; I said, 'Thank you.'

grounded_facts: Hillard is killed by an alien that bores into her head during the ambush.
memories.memory_text: I saw the alien shoot out of the brush and land on Hillard, and I slammed my foot on the pedal, but then I watched it bore into her head before St Just blew it away.

grounded_facts: The vehicle goes off-road and crashes down multiple terraced drops to escape pursuing aliens.
memories.memory_text: I swerved the jeep off the road and down the terraced slope, crashing from ledge to ledge to escape the aliens chasing us.

grounded_facts: Multiple aliens launch a sudden attack on the vehicle as it traverses the garden, initiating a chase.
memories.memory_text: I was driving the vehicle through the garden when multiple aliens launched a sudden attack, jumping at us from above and around, and I had to swerve and keep moving to evade them as we tried to put distance between us and the creatures.

grounded_facts: The vehicle reaches the end of the garden where three paths diverge, requiring a directional decision.
memories.memory_text: I saw that the garden path ended and split into three open halls, and I knew we had to choose one fast.

grounded_facts: Ripley asks which way to go when reaching a junction in the garden paths.
memories.memory_text: I asked the others which way we should go because I didn't know the right path.

grounded_facts: The crew uses a platform jeep to cross the large garden area, transitioning from one end to the other under increasing threat.
memories.memory_text: I was driving the platform jeep across the garden, trying to get us out under that growing threat, swerving to keep control as the vehicle bounced along.

grounded_facts: The crew discovers a large, unexpected growth of cannabis plants while crossing the garden in a vehicle.
memories.memory_text: I saw it suddenly—a huge field of cannabis plants—when we were crossing the garden, and I couldn't believe what we'd stumbled into.

grounded_facts: Ripley stops the jeep because the staircase ahead is too steep to proceed.
memories.memory_text: I saw the staircase ahead and realized it was too steep for the jeep, so I slammed the brakes and brought us to a halt.

grounded_facts: St Just provides covering fire to protect the crew during their escape.
memories.memory_text: I saw St Just firing his guns nonstop to hold back the aliens, mowing them down even as his weapons ran dry.

grounded_facts: The crew flees the garden sector under alien attack, reaching a door to escape.
memories.memory_text: I was running with the crew as we fled the garden sector, and I remember being the last to reach the door before it closed.

grounded_facts: A coordinated alien assault in the hall results in decompression and crew casualties.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the hall burst open suddenly, everything getting sucked into space, and felt the pressure slam me into the closing door.

grounded_facts: Ripley begins hearing psychic signals from the alien hive, sensing the queen's pain.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Ripley begins hearing psychic signals from the alien hive, sensing the queen's pain.

grounded_facts: Ripley throws Call out of harm's way as aliens emerge from the floor.
memories.memory_text: I saw the aliens burst through the floor and I grabbed Call, hurling her down the corridor to keep her safe.

grounded_facts: Ripley is overwhelmed and dragged into the floor panels by aliens after pushing Call to safety.
memories.memory_text: After throwing Call clear, I was overwhelmed by the aliens; they slammed me down and dragged me under the floor while I was still weak and struggling.

grounded_facts: Aliens breach the floor and seize Ripley during a corridor confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I was grabbed when aliens burst up through the floor, and I remember them dragging my unconscious body down under the panels.

grounded_facts: Call helps Ripley up after she is injured by the door impact.
memories.memory_text: I was dazed after the door hit me, and I felt Call come back to help me up, supporting me when I could barely stand on my own.

grounded_facts: Ripley is carried unconscious through air vents by aliens, regaining partial awareness.
memories.memory_text: I was slammed against the door during decompression and lost consciousness; I remember struggling briefly as the aliens overpowered me, and then coming to only dimly while being carried — my body felt heavy and unresponsive, my thoughts foggy.

grounded_facts: Ripley is slammed against the closing door during decompression, suffering a head injury.
memories.memory_text: I was the last to escape when the decompression hit, and I got sucked backward, slamming hard into the closing door—the impact knocked me out, and I remember struggling to regain consciousness, still feeling groggy afterward.

grounded_facts: Ripley is captured and fully webbed by the aliens, left hanging from the ceiling in a cocooned position.
memories.memory_text: I was carried up by the aliens and completely wrapped in resin, left hanging from the ceiling while I struggled to break free.

grounded_facts: Upon regaining consciousness, Ripley sees the Alien Queen lying below, surrounded by attendants and in visible distress.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Alien Queen lying on her back below me, her belly swollen and distended as she was surrounded by attendants and appeared to be in visible distress.

grounded_facts: Gediman explains that the Queen has multiple reproductive systems and can self-impregnate, making egg-laying an immature phase.
Gediman shares his knowledge of the Queen's asexual reproduction and self-impregnation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gediman explain that the Queen has multiple reproductive systems and can self-impregnate, completing an asexual cycle with six sets of ovaries, and that egg-laying is just an immature phase.

grounded_facts: After witnessing the Queen's suffering and learning the truth, Ripley vows to escape the chamber.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Queen suffering down there, her belly moving as she shrieked and thrashed—I realized what was happening, and I knew I had to get out. I started fighting my bonds and screamed that I was getting the fuck out of there.

grounded_facts: The crew arrives at the loading dock and prepares to board the Betty for immediate departure.
memories.memory_text: I saw the crew rush into the loading dock and run on board the Betty, preparing for immediate departure.

grounded_facts: The crew's organized movement to the loading dock and boarding of the Betty under time pressure.
memories.memory_text: I inferred the crew was rushing to board the Betty under time pressure, knowing atmospheric entry would make escape harder.

grounded_facts: Wren holds a gun to Call's back and threatens to kill her if others resist.
Wren emerges and holds a gun to Call's back, threatening to kill her if others resist.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wren grab Call and hold a gun to her back, and I heard him threaten to shoot her if anyone resisted.

grounded_facts: DiStephano refuses Wren's order to disarm the others and instead aims at Wren.
memories.memory_text: I saw DiStephano refuse Wren's order and aim his weapon at Wren instead.

grounded_facts: The Alien Queen gives birth to a unique white newborn, initiating a massacre in the waste tank.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the Alien Queen's belly burst open and blood spraying everywhere, and then everything went silent as the white newborn appeared.

grounded_facts: The Alien Queen's abdomen bursts open, releasing a new, unique creature.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Alien Queen's abdomen burst open and something new emerge — a large, white alien unlike any I'd seen before, with spider-like legs and red veins running across its head.

grounded_facts: The newborn alien attacks and drains a soldier's blood, killing him.
memories.memory_text: I watched the newborn alien leap onto a soldier and kill him, driving its tongue into his throat and draining his blood until his body went lifeless.

grounded_facts: Wren takes Call hostage and demands control of the ship, leading to a tense confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Wren was trying to take control of the ship by holding Call hostage and forcing the robot to land it.

grounded_facts: Call directly opposes Wren's intention to bring the aliens to Earth.
memories.memory_text: I heard Call say 'No she's not,' standing firmly against Wren's plan to bring the aliens to Earth.

grounded_facts: Johner ridicules Wren's belief that he can control the aliens.
memories.memory_text: I remember Johner mocking Wren, asking if he'd been paying attention, clearly ridiculing his belief that he could control the aliens.

grounded_facts: Purvis launches himself at Wren, initiating a violent struggle.
memories.memory_text: I saw Purvis launch himself at Wren, screaming, starting a violent struggle that erupted out of nowhere.

grounded_facts: An alien bursts from Purvis's chest into Wren's skull, killing both.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the alien burst from Purvis's chest and shoot straight into Wren's skull, killing them both in an instant.

grounded_facts: Ripley tears free from her restraints after the newborn attacks a soldier.
memories.memory_text: I tore my arm free and then pulled myself completely loose from the restraints when the newborn attacked the soldier, plunging down into the pool to escape it.

grounded_facts: Ripley retrieves a fallen soldier's rifle from the pool.
memories.memory_text: I stood up from the pool, covered in blood, and grabbed the soldier's rifle to arm myself.

grounded_facts: Ripley shoots holes in the tank wall and smashes through to escape.
memories.memory_text: I shot at the tank wall, seeing light come through the holes, and smashed through to escape, firing all the while to keep the newborn and other aliens back.

grounded_facts: Call defends herself against a leaping newborn alien by deploying a hidden blade that impales and kills it.
memories.memory_text: I watched Call flick her wrist and deploy a hidden blade that impaled the leaping newborn alien, killing it as it flew right onto the stiletto.

grounded_facts: A newborn alien attacks the crew aboard the Betty, leading to chaotic evasion and combat.
memories.memory_text: I saw the newborn alien lunge at Call and the crew scrambling to evade it, with Johner shooting and chaos breaking out as we all tried to stay alive.

grounded_facts: Ripley quickly climbs up a vertical air shaft to evade pursuing aliens, using a pipe to break a steam line that slows the aliens down.
Ripley rips out a superheated pole, causing a burst of steam that impedes the aliens chasing her in the vent shaft.
memories.memory_text: I kicked open the vent grate and climbed up the vertical shaft fast, using a pipe to pull myself up, and when I saw the aliens closing in, I grabbed that superheated pole despite the pain and ripped it out to release a burst of steam that slowed them down.

memories.memory_text: I told Elgyn I already checked the cargo trucks an hour ago — he didn’t have to look at me like that. I could feel the vibration from the music in my chest, but I stayed steady on the harvester.
Vriess called out for me to adjust the generator plugs while he was still under the machine — I remember the clang of metal as I moved, knowing one mistake could fuck everything up.
I don't like army. I said it out loud because the tension was crawling up my neck—everything too clean, too quiet, like we were walking into a trap.
When Wren said 'Ripley,' I felt my breath catch—something sharp and sudden inside me, like a wire pulled tight. I couldn't look away.
I told Wren he was the one who thought he could control it, and when Elgyn asked if we could move, I pointed at Wren and said he knew the way — I wasn’t letting him hide behind silence.
I got the door open, hands shaking on the controls, and then Ripley was just there—standing in the doorway, calm like death, and I didn't know if she was going to help or make it worse.
I told Ripley to fuck off when she said to leave Purvis behind — I couldn't just walk away from a man who didn't even know what was inside him.
I suggested freezing Purvis on the Betty so the doctor could remove the thing inside him later — it was the only way to save him without risking everyone now.

I tried to run in to help the soldiers, but Ripley grabbed me hard and wouldn't let go—I screamed at her, fought to break free, but by the time she let go, all I could see were body parts scattered across the room.
They were planning to lure the aliens toward us—Wren mentioned the failsafe, and suddenly I realized they might use me as bait, left exposed just to draw them in, and no one said otherwise.
I asked Ripley if she was okay when she held her head, and then I said we should get moving—there was no time to waste in that overgrown maze.
I shouted 'St Just!' and issued a ship warning to evacuate the sector, but he just walked toward the aliens, calm, saying he was bored, so I kept warning even as the others moved out.
I grabbed Ripley to help her up after she slammed into the door, her head dazed, and I asked if she could walk—she didn’t even answer, just stood there like she was hearing something I couldn’t.
Ripley grabbed me and threw me fifteen feet down the corridor. Then the aliens came up through the floor and surrounded her. I saw them drag her under while I was still getting up.

I hesitated, looking back at the chamber, knowing we were leaving Ripley behind—I could still see her being covered in that resin, helpless. Purvis grabbed my arm and pulled me forward, but all I could think was, it's not right.
I felt the cold press of Wren's gun against my back, just below my shoulder blades, and heard him snarl that he'd put a bullet where my brain is if anyone moved.
Purvis convulsed in the corner, eyes wide, and then something erupted from his chest—fast and violent—flying straight into Wren's skull, making me flinch and brace for impact.
I flicked my wrist just in time—the blade snapped out and the creature impaled itself, screaming onto the steel. Blood sprayed my face and the stiletto melted inside it, but I didn’t let go.
I announced the airlock doors were closing—protocol demanded it—but I didn't move to stop them, even when Ripley screamed.

I remember the ship's voice cutting through my focus—'Braking system nonfunctional. Collision imminent'—and my hands still moving, trying to stabilize the descent even as Johner yelled we had seconds left.
I shouted 'NOW!!!' as loud as I could—Vriess had to move, we had no time left.
I saw the Akiriga loom overhead, massive and closing fast, and when Vriess shouted, I snapped back—'I am!'—already gripping the controls, scanning for clearance.
I saw Ripley on the hatch, slamming her fist, barely holding on while that thing crawled toward her—I didn’t hesitate, I shoved Johner aside and hit the release sequence myself.
The panel beside me exploded in sparks while the ship shook—I heard the banging above, then Johner shouting about Ripley, and I knew we were coming apart at the seams.
I jumped back into the pilot's seat, fighting the wheel as the Betty scraped through the trees—I could feel the vibrations shaking through my hands, and I knew we were coming down hard.
Ripley said 'Hit it,' and I threw on the thrusters—flame surged forward, the ship rocketed ahead, and for a second, I didn't know if we'd survive the speed.
I took the whiskey from Christie, felt the weight of it in my hand, and drank—Vriess’s words made it clear we were all in this together, and for once, I didn’t have to run or fight alone.
I handed the bottle to Ripley and asked her what we should do now—her not knowing felt like freedom, not failure, and standing there, I realized we both had a future to figure out.

relations.relation_summary: The relationship between CALL and Johner is predominantly defined by mutual hostility and antagonism. Social relationship evidence reveals a pattern of verbal and physical aggression: Johner repeatedly insults CALL, calling her a 'talking machine' and accusing her of being a spy, while also demonstrating lethal intent by pointing a gun at her temple. CALL responds with verbal insults and physically pushes Johner aside during a crisis, indicating reciprocal hostility. Despite this animosity, there is evidence of reluctant cooperation under extreme conditions—during the ship's collision, CALL directs Johner in emergency actions, suggesting a temporary, situational alignment of goals. Their joint experiences, such as being herded into the mess hall by soldiers and the confrontation over opening the hatch for Ripley, highlight their opposing instincts—CALL favoring inclusion and action, Johner prioritizing caution and control. The power struggle peaks when Johner threatens CALL with a firearm, asserting dominance, yet they continue to operate in the same high-stakes environment. The evidence is insufficient to confirm any meaningful evolution toward trust or alliance; instead, the relationship remains tense, marked by conflict punctuated by episodic, necessity-driven coordination.

The relationship between Call and Ripley is defined by intense ambivalence, oscillating between hostility and cooperation under extreme circumstances. Initially, Call harbors deep suspicion toward Ripley, viewing her as a biological threat due to her connection with the Aliens; this leads to multiple instances of attempted violence, including Call trying to stab Ripley while she sleeps and explicitly stating her intent to kill her. Ripley, in turn, responds with physical aggression—strangling Call and confronting her with lethal intent—demonstrating reciprocal hostility rooted in distrust of Call's motives. Despite this antagonism, both characters are repeatedly forced into collaboration to survive. They jointly participate in critical events such as escaping the harvester, activating the ship’s destruction sequence, and battling the Alien threat, where they exchange resources, provide cover, and physically rescue each other. Key moments like Ripley protecting Call by hurling her to safety, Call dragging Ripley into shelter, and their final shared gaze at the dying Newborn underscore a complex dynamic of mutual reliance. Emotional tones shift from cold dismissal and fear to brief instances of physical intimacy and comfort, such as Ripley’s gentle touch on Call’s forehead and her reassurance during crisis. The relationship evolves from outright enmity toward a fragile alliance forged through shared trauma, culminating in a quiet, wordless cooperation at the film’s end. However, the undercurrent of suspicion never fully dissipates, as evidenced by Call’s bitter commentary on Ripley’s humanity and Ripley’s lingering emotional ambiguity. Ultimately, their bond is not one of trust or affection, but of necessity—survival demands cooperation despite unresolved conflict.

memories.memory_text: I felt it moving inside me, and I couldn't stop scratching at my chest—my fingers tearing into my skin, blood spilling over, but I couldn't stop.

I felt the laser cut into my chest, slicing through skin and muscle while I was still half-covered in that cold, sticky slime—I could hear voices, someone saying 'There she is' as they pulled the thing out of me.
I woke in pain and grabbed the surgeon’s arm—felt it give under my grip, heard him scream, bones cracking—before everything went black again.
I touched my chest and felt the ridge of the scar—cold, familiar, but wrong. It was the same scar, but I wasn’t the same woman.
I looked at my forearm and saw the number 8 inked into my skin—sharp, deliberate. Not a mark I made. Not mine.
I grabbed Wren by the throat—fast, hard—pulled his face to mine and demanded, 'Why?' My hands were crushing him, my eyes burning, but I didn't know what I was asking for.
I was in the corner, stunned from the shock, the taste of metal in my mouth. I sat there, barely moving, and whispered 'Why...?'—not to him, not to anyone. Just the word hanging in the air.
I flipped through those stupid picture cards—house, dog, boat—like I was some lab rat, and I could feel their eyes on me, judging, not seeing me, just the thing they made.

I looked at the fork in my hand, and the word came back—'fork'—but it wasn't just about the object. It was the first crack, the moment the memories started pushing through. Then I asked if it grows, and when he said yes, I knew: it's a queen.

Wren talked about harnessing them, about benefits, like they could control it. But I know better. I said it out loud—'It's a cancer. You can't teach it tricks.' And then I whispered 'Them...' because it's not just one. It's never just one.

I stepped off the ship onto the grated platform, the soldiers standing like statues, and I felt the weight of their eyes—cold, mechanical—scanning us, judging us. Something in the air here was tight, wrong, like the place was holding its breath.
I hit him in the chest and he flew back ten feet, crashing into chairs. They didn’t understand—I was still in control, even when they came at me.
I said, 'He... smells.' Then I told him to get away from me.

I stood in the doorway, didn't move, didn't flinch—just let it see me. I felt its gaze lock onto mine, and for a second, I let myself go quiet, like offering myself. Then it lunged, and I spun hard, grabbed its weight, and threw it like I meant to break it.

It was on me fast, claws in my skin, that piston tongue snapping at my face—slime and heat and pressure. I locked my arm around its head and pulled back until something tore. I felt it give. I didn't let go. I couldn't.
I caught the scent—something sour and wrong beneath his sweat—and the moment I cocked my head, I knew. There’s a thing inside him, growing. I can smell it.
When he asked who I was, I told him straight—'I'm the monster's mother'—and walked away. No need to explain. He felt it.
I grabbed Call and held her tight when she tried to rush in—she was shaking, screaming to help the soldiers, but I knew we couldn't risk it. The aliens were already tearing them apart.
I saw an alien rise in front of the soldier remains after the noise stopped. Call tried to move, I held her back. Wren said he could freeze the aliens if we lured them to the failsafe.
I held my head, shutting my eyes against a sudden wave of pain and disorientation when we entered The Garden—something about this place hit me hard, like a signal I couldn't ignore.

I sat in the driver's seat, staring blankly at unfamiliar controls until Call turned the ignition—I felt the hum of the electric jeep beneath me as I pushed it forward, fast, down the narrow path through the overgrown dark.
I was slammed backward by the blast, the door crashing into my head as it sealed—then the vacuum pulled at me, and I couldn't move, dazed, ears ringing, barely holding on.
I heard them before I saw them—the queen's pain echoing in my skull, the hive pulsing around us—and then they burst up through the floor, dragging me under before I could fight back.
They carried me up the walls like I was nothing, spitting that burning resin from their backs, gluing me in place while I could barely move.
Hanging there, stuck to the ceiling with my legs encased, I saw no eggs—nothing. Just me, alone, and that silence meant something worse was happening.
I tore at the bindings, my arm straining until I felt it rip free—skin, muscle, something giving way—as the newborn pushed out of the queen in a burst of blood and silence.
I saw the rifle dangling from the soldier’s side, still twitching in the corner—my only chance—and I knew I had to move fast before that thing turned and the noise started again.
I grabbed the pole even though it burned my hand—steam exploded from the wall and I kept climbing, knowing the aliens were right behind me.
I saw the airlock doors starting to close and I didn't hesitate—I threw myself through the window, glass tearing into me, but I had to get through.
I saw the airlock doors closing, Betty disappearing inside, and I ran—faster than I thought I could—with the sound of aliens slamming behind me.
I leapt off the platform and dropped through the narrowing gap just in time, then crashed hard onto the Auriga—I felt the impact slam through my body, and I couldn't move at first.

I was on my knees, crawling toward the hatch, every breath like fire—then I saw it through the window, the newborn appearing in the docking bay. Sky wide open below, ship breaking apart, and I knew I had to move or die.
I reached the hatch, fingers slipping as I clawed at the seal—so close—and then the glass exploded as it dropped down, landing between me and the way out.
I was thrown straight up, the force slamming through me as I clung to the hatch—my body screaming, the void pulling, but I wouldn't let go. Not me. Not the baby.
I was hanging on, slamming my fist against the hatch, knowing the newborn was crawling toward me — I could hear it, feel the ship shudder under its weight.

I was thrown off the ship, grabbed the newborn's tentacle to hold on, then climbed an external grate toward the hatch. The hatch opened, Call appeared with a grenade launcher and fired, and I reached her just before it closed.
I was hanging onto Call, barely holding on, my body spent and shaking — the hatch was buckling, something pounding on it, and all I could do was move, just get us forward.
The ship slammed into the trees, jolting hard — I remember the impact throwing us, the world upside down, and knowing I had to stay conscious, had to stay on my feet no matter how much it hurt.
I stood at the edge of the cliff, staring at the city lights below, and when Call asked what we should do, I could only say I was a stranger here myself.

memories.memory_text: I told Elgyn the other harvester was a total fucking write-off—he wanted both running, but I knew it wasn’t happening. I could feel the machine’s dead weight under me, the burnt-out wiring, no chance in hell.
I heard the clunk just before the dolly dropped—someone fucked with the release, nearly crushed me. Didn’t see who, but I know it was deliberate. Goddamn prick.

I rolled past those stiff soldiers, last of the crew, and shot a look at one of them — 'Wanna check the chair?' — because of course they’d eye the damn thing like it’s hiding contraband. Felt the weight of their stare, same as always.
I grabbed a stack of bills, brought it up to my nose — caught that sharp, clean paper-and-ink smell. Felt right. Real. Better than the recycled air in this tin can dock.
I was moving down the hall, slow and careful, when I saw a drop of alien blood eating through the ceiling right above me—I barely rolled out of the way in time.
I flattened my chair and slipped under that closing door, heart pounding—no time to think, just move, and I made it before whatever was chasing me got through.
I tore that thing apart with my bare hands, felt its tongue rip out, and roared — they all saw it. They had to see what I can do.
I stood up, looked them in the eye, and asked who I had to fuck to get off this boat — not begging, just cutting through the bullshit. They needed to know I wasn't asking for permission.
I said it was a bad risk to bring Purvis with us after Ripley said he had a parasite inside him. I reminded Call we were supposed to stop them from spreading.
I realized they knew it was a trap because they couldn't smell the fear—aliens don't move without it, and we had none to give.
I held up a ripe pear and asked if they had something against spam—felt good to jab at the tension, even if no one laughed.
I tossed the pear aside, hauled myself into the truck, and told everyone to move quickly and quietly—no time for mistakes.
Di Stephano grabbed me and hauled me out of the jeep when the aliens were closing in—no time to argue, just move.
I told the crew we'd need Call to open the Betty's hatch—I could feel the clock ticking, atmosphere burning in, and the only way out was through her interface.
I scrambled back, knocking shit over, trying to get away from that thing—then it vanished. I remember yelling, 'Where'd it go?' heart pounding, not knowing where it would come from next.
I saw it—something was clinging to the ship, and I knew right then we weren't shaking it off that easy.
I punched the button when the 'CALL NOW!!!' alert lit up—no time to think, just react.
I saw the Akiriga loom over us, massive and dark, and I shouted a warning—no time to think, just react.
I shouted at Johner to strap in—he was still gawking at the screen while we were coming apart. We were going down hard and he wasn't even buckled.
I screamed at Call to kill thrust—she had us rocketing forward and we were about to tear through the trees. Had to stop the burn before we became kindling.
I looked at Call and said she wouldn't want to answer any official questions either — we both knew what that meant. No safe return, no debriefings, just running.
I told her we were on Earth, for Chrissake — plenty of places to get lost. Didn't say it like it was good news. Just the facts.
